106: 
107: Like Lean's own expressions, we use the locally nameless
108: representation for this abstract syntax.
109: See this [paper](https://chargueraud.org/research/2009/ln/main.pdf)
110: for details.
111: 
112: We leave placeholders for type annotations only for constants
113: (`.const`), operations (`.op`), binders (`.abs`, `.quant`), and free
114: variables (`.fvar`).
115: 
116: LExpr is parameterized by `LExprParamsT`, which includes arbitrary metadata,
117: user-allowed type annotations (optional), and special metadata to attach to
118: `Identifier`s. Type inference adds any missing type annotations.
119: -/
120: inductive LExpr (T : LExprParamsT) : Type where
121:   /-- A constant (in the sense of literals). -/
122:   | const   (m: T.base.Metadata) (c: LConst)
123:   /-- A built-in operation, referred to by name. -/
124:   | op      (m: T.base.Metadata) (o : Identifier T.base.IDMeta) (ty : Option T.TypeType)
125:   /-- A bound variable, in de Bruijn form. -/
126:   | bvar    (m: T.base.Metadata) (deBruijnIndex : Nat)
127:   /-- A free variable, with an optional type annotation. -/
128:   | fvar    (m: T.base.Metadata) (name : Identifier T.base.IDMeta) (ty : Option T.TypeType)
129:   /-- An abstraction, where `ty` the is (optional) type of bound variable. -/
130:   | abs     (m: T.base.Metadata) (ty : Option T.TypeType) (e : LExpr T)
131:   /-- A quantified expression, where `k` indicates whether it is universally or
132:   existentially quantified, `ty` is the type of bound variable, and `trigger` is
133:   a trigger pattern (primarily for use with SMT). -/
134:   | quant   (m: T.base.Metadata) (k : QuantifierKind) (ty : Option T.TypeType) (trigger: LExpr T) (e : LExpr T)
135:   /-- A function application. -/
136:   | app     (m: T.base.Metadata) (fn e : LExpr T)
137:   /-- A conditional expression. This is a constructor rather than a built-in
138:   operation because it occurs so frequently. -/
139:   | ite     (m: T.base.Metadata) (c t e : LExpr T)
140:   /-- An equality expression. This is a constructor rather than a built-in
141:   operation because it occurs so frequently. -/
142:   | eq      (m: T.base.Metadata) (e1 e2 : LExpr T)
143: 
144: instance [Repr T.base.Metadata] [Repr T.TypeType] [Repr T.base.IDMeta] : Repr (LExpr T) where
145:   reprPrec e prec :=
146:     let rec go : LExpr T → Std.Format
147:       | .const m c =>
148:         f!"LExpr.const {repr m} {repr c}"
149:       | .op m o ty =>
150:         match ty with
151:         | none => f!"LExpr.op {repr m} {repr o} none"
152:         | some ty => f!"LExpr.op {repr m} {repr o} (some {repr ty})"
153:       | .bvar m i => f!"LExpr.bvar {repr m} {repr i}"
154:       | .fvar m name ty =>
155:         match ty with
156:         | none => f!"LExpr.fvar {repr m} {repr name} none"
157:         | some ty => f!"LExpr.fvar {repr m} {repr name} (some {repr ty})"
158:       | .abs m ty e =>

@[grind =] theorem subset_def {l₁ l₂ : List α} : l₁ ⊆ l₂ ↔ ∀ {a : α}, a ∈ l₁ → a ∈ l₂ := .rfl

@[simp] theorem nil_subset (l : List α) : [] ⊆ l := nofun

@[simp] theorem Subset.refl (l : List α) : l ⊆ l := fun _ i => i

theorem Subset.trans {l₁ l₂ l₃ : List α} (h₁ : l₁ ⊆ l₂) (h₂ : l₂ ⊆ l₃) : l₁ ⊆ l₃ :=
  fun _ i => h₂ (h₁ i)

instance : Trans (fun l₁ l₂ => Subset l₂ l₁) (Membership.mem : List α → α → Prop) Membership.mem :=
  ⟨fun h₁ h₂ => h₁ h₂⟩

instance : Trans (Subset : List α → List α → Prop) Subset Subset :=
  ⟨Subset.trans⟩

theorem subset_cons_self (a : α) (l : List α) : l ⊆ a :: l := fun _ => Mem.tail _

theorem subset_of_cons_subset {a : α} {l₁ l₂ : List α} : a :: l₁ ⊆ l₂ → l₁ ⊆ l₂ :=
  fun s _ i => s (mem_cons_of_mem _ i)

@[simp] theorem subset_cons_of_subset (a : α) {l₁ l₂ : List α} : l₁ ⊆ l₂ → l₁ ⊆ a :: l₂ :=
  fun s _ i => .tail _ (s i)

theorem cons_subset_cons {l₁ l₂ : List α} (a : α) (s : l₁ ⊆ l₂) : a :: l₁ ⊆ a :: l₂ :=
  fun _ => by simp only [mem_cons]; exact Or.imp_right (@s _)

@[simp] theorem cons_subset : a :: l ⊆ m ↔ a ∈ m ∧ l ⊆ m := by
  simp only [subset_def, mem_cons, or_imp, forall_and, forall_eq]

@[simp] theorem subset_nil {l : List α} : l ⊆ [] ↔ l = [] :=
  ⟨fun h => match l with | [] => rfl | _::_ => (nomatch h (.head ..)), fun | rfl => Subset.refl _⟩

theorem eq_nil_of_subset_nil {l : List α} : l ⊆ [] → l = [] := subset_nil.mp

theorem map_subset {l₁ l₂ : List α} (f : α → β) (h : l₁ ⊆ l₂) : map f l₁ ⊆ map f l₂ :=
  fun x => by simp only [mem_map]; exact .imp fun a => .imp_left (@h _)

grind_pattern map_subset => l₁ ⊆ l₂, map f l₂ where

  l₁ =/= List.filter _ _

theorem filterMap_subset {l₁ l₂ : List α} (f : α → Option β) (H : l₁ ⊆ l₂) :

  simp only [mem_filterMap]
  rintro ⟨a, h, w⟩

theorem subset_append_right (l₁ l₂ : List α) : l₂ ⊆ l₁ ++ l₂ := fun _ => mem_append_right _

@[simp] theorem subset_append_of_subset_left (l₂ : List α) : l ⊆ l₁ → l ⊆ l₁ ++ l₂ :=

fun s => Subset.trans s <| subset_append_right _ _

@[simp] theorem append_subset {l₁ l₂ l : List α} :
    l₁ ++ l₂ ⊆ l ↔ l₁ ⊆ l ∧ l₂ ⊆ l := by simp [subset_def, or_imp, forall_and]

theorem replicate_subset {n : Nat} {a : α} {l : List α} : replicate n a ⊆ l ↔ n = 0 ∨ a ∈ l := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih => simp +contextual [replicate_succ, ih, cons_subset]

  induction l with
  | nil => simp

    solve_by_elim

  simp [subset_def]

@[simp] theorem subset_reverse {l₁ l₂ : List α} : l₁ ⊆ reverse l₂ ↔ l₁ ⊆ l₂ := by
